quest.title: Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom
quest.description: The second day's tests have come to a successful close. After a joyful banquet, the third day finally arrives. It's time to test the story's ending...

chapter.num: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Part III
chapter.title: Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom

talks.objective: Wait until the following day (08:00 – 10:00)

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Ah, that explains the loud noise I heard outside. So it was Dvalin who fell into the river...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Considering his size, the fact that he broke a single window and not the entire wall seems like a feat of magic in itself.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Thanks for helping with the repairs, you two. This place looks as good as new now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that count as a great feat of alchemy, then?

talks.objective: Go to the Knights of Favonius Headquarters and participate in the test

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we made it. Time for round tw— Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Was this bubble this color before? Is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I'm not sure. It was like this when I came to check on things this morning.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's the Abyss...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What? That... That can't be! How would the power of the Abyss even get in there?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: #You sure know your stuff, {NICKNAME}. That's where my head went too. But, I don't know... something is different about this power.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: What does that mean?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: It seems to be in an "embryonic state." Like an egg that hasn't hatched, the dark clouds before a storm, or... an omen before disaster strikes.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Of course, the world within the magic bubble is imaginary, so the same should be true of this Abyssal power... at least for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You created this magic, right, Alice? Do you have any idea what's going on here?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: New magic does often come with its issues. So, I can't say I'm entirely surprised something like this would crop up.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: As for a solution, however, I'm afraid I need more information first.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: One thing is for certain, at least... Given the current threat, we'll have to close off the bubble to event participants.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: My apologies, Miss Alice. I know you've made a promise to Klee, but I'm not sure you'll be able to keep it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, have we ever seen Alice look this serious...?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Unprecedented crisis notwithstanding, it's too soon to just throw in the towel. What we should be focusing on is how we're going to fix this.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Are we talking about the Klee situation or the Abyss situation...?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Both! Now, I have my suspicions, but I'll need someone to head into the bubble and confirm a few things.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: It's not like we can avoid going in there, right? We have to nip this crisis in the bud, after all.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I agree. We have to take action.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Alright. I'll go convince Klee to play somewhere else for now and then head right back.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: In the meantime, Nicole, be a dear and keep observing the bubble from out here. Oh, and provide any fixes you can while the rest are inside.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: I don't know, Alice. There are quite a few unknowns here. It's not like I can force people to head in there and take that risk. We angels aren't miracle workers...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: ...You sure about that?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: ...Fine, I'll do what I can. Just be quick, okay? This is your magic, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, guess this is our best option. We're definitely not gonna sit back and watch!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What was today's story meant to be again?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: The part where Barbatos uses the Lyre to summon Abyss-corrupted Dvalin.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Then, everyone joins forces to fight him inside Stormterror's Lair, purges him of Abyssal influence, and there you have it... happy ending.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that sounds like how it happened...

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Well, we've got the gang from back then all here. Let's go in and find out what's happening.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Count me in too. Potential threat or not, if there's even the slightest chance Mondstadt is in danger, I need to get to the bottom of it.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Jean?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: It's nothing. I was just feeling a bit... nostalgic, getting to work together like this again.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Yeah, yesterday felt like that too.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Yes, but that was for fun. That which confronts us now is a real crisis. So, I suppose the memories just... came back to me all at once.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, look at you getting all sentimental! That's a first!

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I... Ahem. Well, I suppose I am a bit too high-strung most of the time.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Hey, don't be embarrassed to say what you feel. I think that's how things should be. It's how we all grow closer.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Besides, the more you open up, the less people will be surprised like Paimon here when you choose to share something.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Just look at Paimon, no filter whatsoever, word vomits whatever comes to mind... And that's what makes her so... endearing and approachable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hah, it's about time you gave Paimon a compliment, Tone-Deaf Bard... Hang on, was that a compliment?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Before we set off, I just want to stress that whatever is happening in the bubble right now is a huge unknown.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: I was able to maintain contact before, but right now, all I can observe within is chaos. So, I imagine communication might be cut off as well.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: It might be difficult for us to guide you, so proceed with caution.

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Don't worry. This isn't our first time leaping head-first into a dangerous situation.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: There's also a last resort I can fall back on if worst comes to worst... Though it would mean all our recent hard work going to waste.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: You mean... destroying the bubble entirely?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Yes. If it comes down to it.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Alright. I'll monitor the situation from outside, and provide whatever external fixes and support I can in the meantime.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Understood. Prepare for the worst, hope for the best. Sound good?

response.speaker: Diluc
response.text: Alright, let's go.

choices.text: ...Might make her angrier than all of Dottore's scheming combined.
It's Abyssal in nature, but also... not a threat?

talks.objective: Enter the anomalous bubble

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, it's Jean!

talks.objective: Enter the anomalous bubble

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... I—Is this Mondstadt?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't we all come in at the same time? Where are the others?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The bubble must be highly unstable right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look! There's Venti... surrounded by a whole bunch of monsters!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We should go help him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, perfect timing. C'mon, let's show these unwelcome guests the door.

talks.objective: Defeat the monsters

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Diluc is over there!

talks.objective: Talk to Venti and go over the current situation

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All good, Venti?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Very much so, thanks to your timely arrival. But, Mondstadt looks like it's in bad shape.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The story's all messed up now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! The city's crawling with Abyssal monsters! It's almost like... we've already lost.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I'm not sure what happened, but the rest of our group might need backup. Let's find them first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good point. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Look, it's Dvalin! Is it just Paimon, or... does he look way worse than back then?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You're right. The corruption has spread throughout his entire body. If we had failed to purify him in real life, I imagine this is what would have become of him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, it looks like something's falling!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: It's his tears...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like the ones we purified in the past?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yes, but at this point... These tears are essentially crystallizations of Abyssal power.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: If left unchecked, they will continuously summon Abyssal monsters, and this disaster will never end.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: We also need to get our hands on one of them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Right, so I can purify it.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: No, this degree of corruption cannot be cleansed. Besides, we need them in their corrupted state if we want to summon Dvalin.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I doubt the pure sound of the lyre can reach him in his current state.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like this whole thing is still gonna end in a confrontation, though. Just like back then...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yes. I wasn't certain before Dvalin showed up, but now I'm sure this situation is more than simple chaos.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: It seems more like... an alternate version of events, and I have some idea of how it came to be.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Well, monsters abound no matter where we look. You choose where to go, and I'll follow.

choices.text: But we should find our companions first.

talks.objective: Collect the tears and find your companions
Defeat the monsters
Collect the tears and find your companions

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Thanks for the help.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I know everything we encounter in this bubble is imaginary, but these monsters sure fight like the real thing. It's a bit too true to life.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Don't worry, as long as we collect Dvalin's tears, we can use this Abyssal power to our advantage.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I see... In that case, let's get moving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Have you seen Varka, by the way? We haven't found him yet.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: No, he might be at the upper levels. Let's search together.

talks.objective: Collect the tears and find your companions
Defeat the monsters
Collect the tears and find your companions

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Phew, made it. Thanks for the assist.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: It looks like Mondstadt is in dire straits... Did you see any Knights or civilians on the way here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Hm, then my initial suspicion could be right... The Knights have abandoned the city and evacuated all civilians to a different location.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A—Abandoned the city...?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: In the face of unrelenting Abyssal attacks, it's possible they had no other choice. But, none of that matters now.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: An empty city has its advantages. We won't need to divert our attention to protecting civilians, for one.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Oh, and this thing... It looks like one of Dvalin's tears. I don't feel good about just leaving it here.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: That happens to be just what we were hoping to find. Let's take it with us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, what about Varka? Have you seen him?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: No, I'm not sure where he is. We'll just have to keep looking.

talks.objective: Defeat the monsters
Collect the tears and find your companions

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Phew, made it. Thanks for the assist.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc

dialogues.speaker: Player

dialogues.speaker: Jean

dialogues.speaker: Jean

dialogues.speaker: Jean

dialogues.speaker: Jean

talks.objective: Collect the tears and find your companions

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—The statue's broken!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: The Grand Master should be over there. C'mon, let's hurry.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Here, I'll draw him for you. Look, this is the bad guy who made a whole bunch of trouble for Daddy. It's all his fault Daddy couldn't make it back this time.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: That big meanie! We should blow him up!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: #That's right, he is a big meanie! But, thanks to the Honorary Knight and {M#his}{F#her} friends, he's not going to be much trouble anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Klee
dialogues.text: Yay! The Honorary Knight is the best!

talks.objective: Go to the plaza in front of the Cathedral

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: We're here to help!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Perfect timing. Let's do this!

talks.objective: Clear out the monsters present
Discuss what to do with everyone

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Looks like we're all back together. Everyone in one piece?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Yes. The Honorary Knight arrived just in time to help us out.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Now that we've collected Dvalin's tears, the monster attacks appear to be easing up, too.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I'm sure you've noticed, Varka, but the city is pretty much a ghost town at this point.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah, we should get out of here. No sense wasting our strength.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: This place should be safe from monster attacks for now, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Anyone there? The communication function bugged out again. Do you copy? It's me, Nicole. Alice just got back too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we can hear you now! What's going on!?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: #When designing this experience, we cut out the part where {NICKNAME} cleanses the Abyssal power, and we didn't think to replace it with a different sequence of events. I think what we're witnessing is a direct result of that.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Alice and I thought the events in the bubble would be independent from each other.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: But since the magic is contained in one place, it appears a causal link has formed between all the events within it...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: And so, because Dvalin was never purified, we've encountered a major bug.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I knew it.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: So, what we're witnessing now is like an alternate version of events where the Honorary Knight never appeared in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Wait but, even if {NICKNAME} never showed up, you could have done something, right, Venti?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The Abyss is a far greater enemy than one person can face. I could have handled that specific situation, sure, but it wouldn't have gone quite so well.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: If I'm not mistaken, you've seen how that version of the story goes yourself, right, Varka? Through the mages' scryglass?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Yeah, it was a kind of... prophecy. It felt so real, I doubt I could ever forget it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: In the end... You were able to seal Dvalin away, but you were wounded in the process.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: But if Dvalin was sealed, how did things get to this point?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Because a seal doesn't solve the root problem. Over time, the Abyss would just grow stronger and stronger, deteriorating Dvalin's consciousness until there was nothing left.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, does that mean what we saw earlier was...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The aftermath of Dvalin breaking free from the seal... That's right. He is in dire straits.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: The power of the Abyss has fused with his flesh and bones. Purifying him now, in this state, is no different than sentencing him to death.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: So, if we want to resolve this crisis...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We have to kill Dvalin.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I know that sounds intense. But remember, this is a fictional world. The real Dvalin is right as rain, and a lot more mellow than this one, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We have our solution, so let's hop to it. Should be a piece of cake for a group like this.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: No time to lose, right? We've got Klee waiting for us, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hahaha, she's playing somewhere else right now, so we do have some time. Of course, the sooner we resolve this the better.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: ...You're right. This is the only way.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I know Dvalin means a lot to you. If this is too hard, you can leave it to us, y'know. No need to scar yourself over a game, right?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I'll be fine. I was... prepared for that possibility back then, too.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Let's go. Stormterror's Lair awaits.

talks.objective: Go to Stormterror's Lair
Go to Stormterror's Lair

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: This is it. Ready, everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Hah. More than.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Of course. I just hope I learned a thing or two since the first time around.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, guess I'm the newbie, huh? Good thing I'm a quick learner, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #What about you, {NICKNAME}? This was your first big fight in Teyvat. Were you nervous back then? How about now?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm not nervous. We've all grown a lot since then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We overcame this challenge once, and we can do it again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon believes in you!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Then let the mournful cries of this lyre, tainted and defiled, summon a familiar now utterly warped.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: You alright, Barbatos?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Turning the surging Abyss into musical notes is no simple task...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: But how could I claim to be the finest bard in Teyvat if I didn't rise to the occasion?

dialogues.speaker: Dvalin
dialogues.text: ■■■■■, ■■■■■... I have heard enough!

dialogues.speaker: Dvalin
dialogues.text: You call me forth ■■■■? ■■■■■■■!

talks.objective: Defeat Dvalin, who has been corrupted by the Abyss
Defeat Dvalin, who has been corrupted by the Abyss

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The bubble crisis is resolved without incident, while Alice and Nicole fix the flaws in the magic to prevent any recurrence of the problems.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Klee doesn't notice a thing, and embarks on a relaxing adventure alongside her mother and Nicole.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Now, the only issue left for the Knights to resolve... might be the window Dvalin broke.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like it was a happy ending after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was kinda like a Choo-Choo Cart ride — it had its fun moments and its thrills. All in all, Paimon had a great time.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Guess it wasn't without some collateral damage, though... Sorry about the window, Jean.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: It's fine. As long as the building itself is intact, I consider that a win. I'll arrange for the window to be replaced at a later date.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: In any case, we were lucky Dvalin arrived when he did. It would have been tricky to deal with a flying opponent otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I suppose I could've created a gust of wind to whisk us up, but I'm not sure our gliders would have survived the process.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Honestly, after everything we faced, I can't believe Alice still decided to bring Klee in there to play. She's a daring one, that's for sure.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: I mean, can we be certain there aren't other bugs that just haven't cropped up yet?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I suppose that speaks to the confidence the mages have in their magical mastery.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Heh, if I know Alice, the whole bubble could've been blown to bits, and Klee still wouldn't have had a single scratch.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Her abilities do speak for themselves, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: So, what now? Anyone down for a drink? My treat.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Hm, sounds like a great idea, but tonight, it's on me. I happen to have a bottle of fine wine set aside just for the expedition team.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Haha, even better. Count me in.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Say no more. You had me at " fine wine"!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Alright, let's head over to my place then. You're coming too, right, Jean?

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: I'm afraid not. There's still a lot of work to do...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: So what? The world's not gonna end if you push it off. C'mon, we never get a chance like this.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Hm, I suppose that wouldn't be a problem... if you head back to headquarters with me after we're done and help make up the work.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Uh, on second thought. How about you just... join us when you're done with that!

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: What about you, Honorary Knight? Gonna tag along?

choices.text: I've still got questions for Alice.

response.speaker: Varka
response.text: Okay. All's well that ends well, am I right? To the bar, haha!

choices.text: I'll wait for her to get back from her adventure with Klee.

talks.objective: Talk with everyone in the Knights of Favonius Headquarters
Talk with everyone in the Knights of Favonius Headquarters
Wait for Alice in the library

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Looking for me?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I'm glad. I wanted to thank you for helping me keep my promise to Klee. She had a splendid time in the bubble.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Nicole came with us to make sure all was in order and prevent any similar incidents from happening in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: *sigh* You live and you learn. It's rare, but even the Dodo-King isn't immune to a small slip-up here and there, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, it's all fixed?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Yes, quite. The recording work is done as well, so now all we have to do is play it on loop.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: It should be smooth sailing from here on out. Anyone and everyone can now enjoy the bubble at their leisure.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Nicole will keep an eye on them, of course.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hmm... I wouldn't put it quite like that. It was more like... a "fate that will not come to pass."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's the difference between the two?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Let us not forget, the courageous dragon slayer in the story? Well, in real life, he had already left on an expedition to Nod-Krai at that time.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Of course, that doesn't mean Dvalin would have escaped his destined death, for another hero would have come along and paid a painful price for victory.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, what we saw in the bubble was what happened after Dvalin broke free from the seal. So, couldn't Varka have been back by then?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Hehe... Dear Paimon, you're free to ponder such questions yourself, of course, but it's of little use to ask them aloud.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Word to the wise — do not lose sleep over all those "what ifs," over the "fates that will not come to pass." It's an exercise in futility.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Those who can observe fate see both the good and the bad of what could have happened.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: But, all that matters is what did happen. Those alternate fates are nowhere near as important as the world that exists in the here and now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Alright...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Ah, you're saying it was as if the bubble itself had become contaminated?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: I suppose some "gunk" could have stuck to my luggage while I was wandering the "border," and got mixed into my magic without me noticing...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Haha, just kidding. I would never be so careless.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: #Your intuition is spot-on, {NICKNAME}. What developed in the bubble was a nascent form of Abyssal power that, if left unchecked, would evolve into the real thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, so it didn't come from outside? It just... appeared out of thin air?

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The Abyss is perilous, cunning, dangerous, obsessive, and most infuriating of all, a complete and utter mystery. I'm sure you've seen for yourself how complex it can be.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The Hexenzirkel has been observing its energies for a long time, and I think Barbeloth's interpretation is the most accurate.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: The essence of the Abyss lies in the hatred carried by all the fates that will not come to pass.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The hatred carried by fate...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: This world is filled with conflicting elements. That one thing should happen signifies that a different possibility has been eliminated.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: These events can be small, almost trivial. I had Sweet Madame for lunch today, for instance. That means the "Alice who chose Tea Break Pancakes instead" is no more.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Of course, they can also be events that threaten the world, such as my friend Rhinedottir's decision to tap into the Abyss. In that instant, the tale of a future in which she remained pure was gone forever.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: So then, the question at the heart of it all is this... Why must these fates be the ones to disappear?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, Paimon gets it. It's hatred that stems from not being chosen.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Precisely. The magic we wove this time involved recreating the past. However, some of the variables we added allowed a certain amount of these "unchosen fates" to come very, very close to reality.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: And, thus, the Abyss showed its teeth. Of course, much like always, it is not existence that it seeks... but the destruction of all.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: In the end, though, it wasn't a huge issue. Things like this happen on the "border" all the time.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: It has quite the victim complex, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: It's obsessed with entering this world at all costs. And that is precisely why we must protect our lives and those of our loved ones.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Because, when you think about it, to exist in this world is to be a spark of luck amidst countless possibilities. How precious is that?

choices.text: Having crossed swords with the Abyss many times...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: Ah, Alice. You're here.

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: I'm truly sorry about this, but per the regulations of the Knights of Favonius, I'm afraid I must send you to confinement.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Whatever for? Things turned out just fine with the magic bubble.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Besides, if that's what this is about... Shouldn't Nicole come along, too?

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: It's not about the bubble. We received word that a number of fish have been injured as a result of explosions near Starfell Lake...

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: As I'm sure you're well aware, fish blasting is strictly prohibited.

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Oh dear...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Run, Klee! Save yourself!

response.speaker: Jean
response.text: She's already inside.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Guess it's a day of firsts for the Dodo-King, huh...

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: #...*sob* Farewell forever, {NICKNAME}. You shall never see me again!

choices.text: I'm beginning to think along the same lines too.
No wonder the Abyss is so full of hatred.
The Abyssal power inside the bubble was far too real...
That was "fate" before we changed it, right?

talks.objective: Additional

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Oh, I think I saw Jean on the other side of the city. I was going to head over after clearing out these monsters. We should go help her.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Good idea.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: In that case, there's no time to waste. Let's head to the Cathedral.

dialogues.speaker: Jean
dialogues.text: Ah, right. I remember seeing Diluc on the other side of the city. We should go help him first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like a plan. Let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Better to find him soon than later. The Grand Master is an exceptional warrior, but this is the Abyss we're dealing with. You can never be too careful.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alice loves going to the library. Let's wait for her there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, looks like it's been fixed already.
